Since the accident, he has had difficulty lifting objects above shoulder level.

He complains of severe pain on the left side of his chest, exacerbated by deep breathing and coughing.
He denies loss of consciousness, headache, or vomiting.

encounters.cc: Continued respiratory distress and chest wall instability following scaffold fall

lines: Continued respiratory distress and chest wall instability following scaffold fall

Following ED evaluation for a scaffold fall, this 49-year-old with shoulder pathology and nephrolithiasis complains of severe pain on the left side of his chest, exacerbated by deep breathing and coughing.
- Rotator cuff tear of right shoulder (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Chronic right shoulder rotator cuff pathology
The patient's past medical history is significant for hypertension.
Smoking: Former smoker, 15 pack-years, quit 3 years ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks per week).
He is in moderate respiratory distress with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute.
His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, and pulse is 110 beats per minute.
On examination, there is obvious deformity of the left chest wall with paradoxical movement noted during inspiration.
Auscultation reveals decreased breath sounds over the left lung field.
Chest X-ray confirms multiple rib fractures on the left side with no evidence of pneumothorax.
